title: Why a Booking System Beats a Calendar Link
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Understand the five parts of a complete booking system and the business goal of each.

items.title: No Context
items.description: A raw calendar link tells the prospect nothing about what to expect, who it is for, or what happens next.

items.title: No Qualification
items.description: You do not know why they are booking, what they need help with, or whether they are a good fit.

items.title: No Follow-Up
items.description: After the booking, the prospect may forget, and you have no system to remind or track them.

items.title: Book
items.description: A branded page where prospects pick a convenient 30-minute slot.

items.title: Qualify
items.description: 3-4 useful questions before the booking completes, so you know why they are coming.

items.title: Remind
items.description: One confirmation and timely reminders so they arrive prepared.

items.title: Track
items.description: Each booking becomes an opportunity in your sales pipeline.

items.title: Follow Up
items.description: After the meeting, no-show, cancellation or reschedule, the next step is clear.

keyPoint: A calendar link is a start. A complete booking system helps you know who is coming, why they want to talk, and what needs to happen next. The five stages — Book, Qualify, Remind, Track, Follow Up — turn a random appointment into a managed business process.

actionSteps.title: Write Your Purpose
actionSteps.description: Write the service or offer and the result the call should lead toward in one sentence.

actionSteps.title: Map the Journey
actionSteps.description: Draw the five stages for your own business: Book → Qualify → Remind → Track → Follow Up.

nextLessonTitle: Name the Call and Choose the Best Audience

quizzes.question: What is the main problem with sharing a raw calendar link?

options.option_text: It requires too many clicks to book
It is too expensive to maintain
It provides no context, qualification, or follow-up system
It only works on desktop computers

quizzes.explanation: A raw calendar link tells the prospect nothing about what to expect, collects no qualification information, and provides no follow-up structure. It is a tool, not a system.

quizzes.question: What are the five stages of a complete booking system?

options.option_text: Plan, build, test, launch, measure
Create, share, book, meet, close
Attract, engage, convert, retain, refer
Book, Qualify, Remind, Track, Follow Up

quizzes.explanation: The five stages are Book, Qualify, Remind, Track, Follow Up. Each stage serves a specific business purpose and together they create a complete prospect journey.

quizzes.question: Why is qualification important before the call?

options.option_text: It automatically rejects unsuitable prospects
It replaces the need for a sales pipeline
It reduces the number of bookings you receive
It gives you context so you can prepare and assess fit

quizzes.explanation: Qualification questions give you useful context before the call. You learn what the prospect needs help with, what they have tried, and when they want to act. This helps you prepare and assess fit.

title: Name the Call and Choose the Best Audience
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Define the right call for the right person with a clear benefit and honest expectations.

items.title: Be Specific
items.description: 30-Minute Discovery Call is clear. Free Consultation is vague and attracts unqualified prospects.

items.title: State the Audience
items.description: Explain who should book and what they will get. Promise a conversation, not a free strategy project.

items.title: Set Expectations
items.description: Be honest about duration, format, and next steps. A 30-minute call should not become a 90-minute unpaid strategy session.

items.title: Speaker
items.description: Speaking Engagement Enquiry — discuss audience size, event type, and fit.

items.title: Coach
items.description: Coaching Fit Call — discuss goals, challenges, and programme suitability.

items.title: Consultant
items.description: Systems Discovery Call — discuss current friction, scope, and potential solutions.

items.title: Trainer
items.description: Training Needs Call — discuss learners, outcomes, and delivery format.

items.title: Service Business
items.description: Project Estimate Call — discuss job type, area, timing, and budget range.

keyPoint: The name and description of your call set expectations and attract the right people. Be specific about duration, audience, and outcome. A 30-Minute Discovery Call for [audience] to [result] is more effective than a vague free consultation offer.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Call Type
actionSteps.description: Select the call type that matches your business from the examples.

actionSteps.title: Write the Description
actionSteps.description: Write call name, intended person, key benefit, and desired next step.

actionSteps.title: Set Boundaries
actionSteps.description: Define what the call is and is not. A conversation, not a free project.

quizzes.question: Why is 30-Minute Discovery Call better than Free Consultation?

options.option_text: It allows you to charge for the call
It takes less time to explain
It is specific about duration and purpose, attracting better-fit prospects
It sounds more professional

quizzes.explanation: 30-Minute Discovery Call is specific about duration and purpose. Free Consultation is vague and attracts unqualified prospects who may expect extensive unpaid work.

quizzes.question: What should you promise in a discovery call?

options.option_text: Guaranteed results or outcomes
Unlimited follow-up support
A conversation to explore fit and next steps
A complete strategy or project plan

quizzes.explanation: Promise a conversation, not a free strategy project. Set honest expectations about duration, format, and possible next steps. This protects your time and attracts serious prospects.

quizzes.question: Which call type would suit a consultant best?

options.option_text: Project Estimate Call
Speaking Engagement Enquiry
Training Needs Call
Systems Discovery Call

quizzes.explanation: A Systems Discovery Call is designed for consultants to discuss current friction, scope, and potential solutions. Each business type has a call type matched to their typical client conversation.

title: Create the Appointment Calendar
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Set up a booking calendar with correct host, availability, duration, and meeting location.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Calendars → Calendar Settings → + New Calendar → Personal Booking

items.title: Host
items.description: Select the correct person whose calendar will receive the bookings.

items.title: Duration
items.description: Set to 30 minutes for a discovery call.

items.title: Availability
items.description: Define working hours, available days, and time zone.

items.title: Booking Lead Time
items.description: Prevent last-minute bookings by requiring advance notice (e.g., 24 hours).

items.title: Buffers
items.description: Add buffer time before or after appointments to prevent back-to-back calls.

items.title: Meeting Location
items.description: Set a valid meeting location: video link, phone number, or physical address.

items.title: Blocked Calendars
items.description: Connect your personal calendar so booked times are unavailable.

items.title: Preview the Widget
items.description: Open the public booking URL and check that slots appear correctly.

items.title: Verify Time Zone
items.description: Confirm the displayed time zone matches your target audience.

items.title: Share URL
items.description: Copy the public booking URL for use in your booking page or direct sharing.

keyPoint: A calendar without correct host, availability, and location settings will frustrate prospects and waste your time. Set 30-minute duration, define working hours, add buffers, connect blocked calendars, and always preview before sharing.

actionSteps.title: Create the Calendar
actionSteps.description: Navigate to Calendars → Calendar Settings and create a new Personal Booking calendar.

actionSteps.title: Configure Settings
actionSteps.description: Set host, 30-minute duration, working hours, time zone, buffers, and meeting location.

actionSteps.title: Test Availability
actionSteps.description: Preview the widget and confirm at least one bookable future slot appears with correct time zone.

quizzes.question: Where do you create a new booking calendar?

options.option_text: Opportunities → Pipelines
Automation → Workflows
Calendars → Calendar Settings → + New Calendar → Personal Booking
Sites → Funnels

quizzes.explanation: Booking calendars are created in Calendars → Calendar Settings → + New Calendar → Personal Booking. This is the correct menu path for setting up a discovery call calendar.

quizzes.question: Why should you add buffer time to your calendar?

options.option_text: To make the calendar look more professional
To prevent back-to-back calls and give you preparation time
To reduce the number of bookings you receive
To increase the price of your services

quizzes.explanation: Buffer time prevents back-to-back calls, giving you time to prepare notes, follow up on the previous call, and avoid running late. It protects both your schedule and the prospect's experience.

quizzes.question: What should you check before sharing your booking URL?

options.option_text: The number of social media followers
That at least one bookable future slot appears with correct time zone and location
The calendar color scheme
Your competitor's pricing

quizzes.explanation: Before sharing, verify that slots display correctly, the time zone matches your audience, and the meeting location is set. A broken booking experience destroys trust before the call even happens.

title: Build a Helpful Qualification Form
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Collect useful details without making booking feel like an application.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Sites → Forms → Builder

items.title: Standard Fields
items.description: First name, last name, email, and any needed phone or consent fields.

items.title: Custom Fields
items.description: Map responses to contact custom fields for business challenge, goal, and timing.

items.title: What would you most like help with?
items.description: Reveals the prospect's primary goal and motivation.

items.title: What is your biggest challenge right now?
items.description: Surfaces pain points and current friction.

items.title: When would you like to act on a solution?
items.description: Shows urgency and timeline, helping you prioritize.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Calendars → Calendar Settings → Edit calendar → Forms & Payment → Select Form

items.title: When It Appears
items.description: After the person chooses a slot, before the booking completes.

items.title: Test the Flow
items.description: Complete a test booking and verify answers save to the contact record.

keyPoint: Qualification questions should feel helpful, not like an application. Three simple questions about goals, challenges, and timing give you enough context to prepare. Attach the form to the calendar so it appears after slot selection but before booking completion. Always test that answers save correctly.

actionSteps.title: Create the Form
actionSteps.description: Build a form in Sites → Forms with standard fields and three custom questions.

actionSteps.title: Map Custom Fields
actionSteps.description: Ensure responses map to contact custom fields for challenge, goal, and timing.

actionSteps.title: Attach to Calendar
actionSteps.description: Connect the form to your discovery call calendar in Calendar Settings.

actionSteps.title: Test the Flow
actionSteps.description: Complete a test booking and verify answers appear on the contact record.

quizzes.question: Where do you create a qualification form?

options.option_text: Automation → Workflows
Calendars → Calendar Settings
Opportunities → Pipelines
Sites → Forms → Builder

quizzes.explanation: Qualification forms are created in Sites → Forms → Builder. This is the form builder where you add fields, set requirements, and map responses to contact custom fields.

quizzes.question: When is a calendar-attached custom form displayed?

options.option_text: After choosing a slot, before booking completes
Before the person sees available slots
Only in the confirmation email
After the booking is confirmed

quizzes.explanation: For a calendar with an attached custom form, the form appears after the person chooses a time slot but before the booking is completed. This captures qualification details at the right moment.

quizzes.question: Do form answers prove a prospect is qualified?

options.option_text: No, they provide helpful context but do not replace discussion
Yes, they automatically qualify or disqualify prospects
Yes, if you use conditional form rules
No, they are only for your records

quizzes.explanation: Form answers provide helpful context for preparation and fit assessment, but they do not replace actual discussion. Advanced form rules can disqualify, but do not automatically reject prospects unless the business has approved those rules.

title: Publish a Booking Page
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Make it easy for prospects to understand the offer and book a slot.

items.title: Direct Calendar URL
items.description: Copy the public booking URL from Calendar Settings → Share. Fastest way to start.

items.title: Custom Funnel Page
items.description: Sites → Funnels → Edit step → Add Calendar element. More branded and contextual.

items.title: Headline
items.description: Result-focused headline that speaks to the prospect's need.

items.title: Short Benefit
items.description: One or two sentences explaining what they will get from the call.

items.title: Who It Suits
items.description: Brief description of the ideal person for this call.

items.title: Duration
items.description: Clear statement of call length so they know what to expect.

items.title: Visible Scheduler
items.description: The calendar element should be prominent and easy to use.

items.title: Headline
items.description: Let's talk about what is slowing your business down.

items.title: Body
items.description: Book a 30-minute discovery call to explain your goal and find out whether we can help.

items.title: CTA
items.description: Book your discovery call.

keyPoint: A booking page should explain the offer, set expectations, and make scheduling effortless. Start with the direct calendar URL for speed; add a custom funnel page when you want more branding and context. Always test on mobile and desktop before sharing.

actionSteps.title: Write Your Copy
actionSteps.description: Draft headline, promise, and call-to-action for your booking page.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Route
actionSteps.description: Use the direct calendar URL or build a custom funnel page with the Calendar element.

actionSteps.title: Test Across Devices
actionSteps.description: Open the booking link on mobile and desktop. Confirm it loads and functions correctly.

quizzes.question: What is the fastest way to start sharing your booking page?

options.option_text: Copy the public booking URL from Calendar Settings → Share
Build a custom website from scratch
Hire a designer to create a landing page
Create a social media campaign first

quizzes.explanation: The fastest way is to copy the public booking URL from Calendar Settings → Share. A custom funnel page is optional and can be added later for more branding.

quizzes.question: What should a booking page include?

options.option_text: Pricing for all your services
Testimonials from every past client
Headline, benefit, who it suits, duration, and visible scheduler
Your full company history and team bios

quizzes.explanation: A booking page needs a result-focused headline, short benefit, description of who it suits, clear duration, and a prominent scheduler. Excess information distracts from the booking action.

quizzes.question: When should you build a custom funnel page instead of using the direct URL?

options.option_text: Never, funnel pages are too complex
Always, the direct URL is unprofessional
Only for paid discovery calls
When you want more branding, context, and control over the page design

quizzes.explanation: A custom funnel page is useful when you want branding, additional context, or control over page design. Start with the direct URL for speed; upgrade to a funnel page when it serves your business needs.

title: Confirmation and Reminders
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Help people turn up ready without sending duplicate messages.

items.title: One Source
items.description: Choose one route for confirmations and reminders. Calendar notifications OR workflow emails, not both.

items.title: Email Default
items.description: Email is the default channel. SMS only where contact consent and messaging setup permit.

items.title: Avoid Duplicates
items.description: Check that calendar notifications and workflow actions are not sending the same message twice.

items.title: Immediate Confirmation
items.description: Sent right after booking. Must include date, time, time zone, meeting location, and reschedule option.

items.title: 24-Hour Reminder
items.description: Sent the day before. Reinforces the appointment and reduces no-shows.

items.title: 1-Hour Reminder
items.description: Sent shortly before the call. Final prompt to ensure attendance.

items.title: Confirmation
items.description: Your Discovery Call is booked for [appointment date and time with time zone]. Join here: [meeting link]. Please bring one challenge you'd like to discuss. Need a different time? [reschedule instructions].

items.title: Reminder
items.description: A quick reminder about our discovery call [appointment date/time]. Here's the meeting link: [meeting link].

keyPoint: One confirmation, sensible reminders, and no duplicates. Choose either calendar notifications or workflow emails for each message type. Test every message before going live. A prospect who receives three identical confirmations will not trust your system.

actionSteps.title: Draft Messages
actionSteps.description: Write confirmation and reminder messages with all required details.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Route
actionSteps.description: Decide whether to use calendar notifications or workflow emails for each message type.

actionSteps.title: Test for Duplicates
actionSteps.description: Book a test slot and count how many messages arrive. There should be one confirmation and scheduled reminders only.

quizzes.question: What should you check before switching on appointment emails in a workflow?

options.option_text: That SMS is enabled for all contacts
That the email template looks professional
That you have at least three reminder emails
That calendar notifications won't send the same message as the workflow

quizzes.explanation: Before enabling workflow emails, confirm that calendar notifications are not sending the same message. Duplicate messages make your business look unprofessional and annoy prospects.

quizzes.question: What four details must a confirmation include?

options.option_text: Price, refund policy, terms, and privacy notice
Company history, team bios, testimonials, and case studies
Date/time/time zone, meeting link, what to prepare, and reschedule option
Social media links, blog posts, newsletter signup, and referral program

quizzes.explanation: A confirmation must include date/time/time zone, meeting link or location, what to prepare, and reschedule instructions. These are the practical details a prospect needs to attend prepared.

quizzes.question: When is SMS appropriate for reminders?

options.option_text: Never, SMS is outdated
Only for paid discovery calls
For all contacts by default
Only where contact consent and messaging setup permit

quizzes.explanation: SMS is optional and should only be used where the contact has given consent and your messaging setup supports it. Email is the reliable default channel for confirmations and reminders.

title: Create the Sales Pipeline
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Make every prospect's next action visible with clear pipeline stages.

items.title: Visibility
items.description: See where every prospect is in your sales process at a glance.

items.title: Ownership
items.description: Assign responsibility for moving each prospect to the next stage.

items.title: Action
items.description: Stage names should reflect actions taken, not assumptions about qualification.

items.title: New Enquiry
items.description: Initial contact or interest expressed. Not yet booked.

items.title: Call Booked
items.description: Appointment scheduled. Waiting for the call to happen.

items.title: Call Completed
items.description: Discovery call held. Next step to be determined.

items.title: Proposal Sent
items.description: Quote or proposal delivered. Awaiting response.

items.title: Won / Lost
items.description: Deal closed or prospect disqualified. Record the outcome.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Opportunities → Pipelines

items.title: Name Your Pipeline
items.description: Discovery Calls or similar clear name.

items.title: Assign Owners
items.description: Name the person responsible for updating each stage.

items.title: Test Movement
items.description: Create a test opportunity and move it through all stages.

keyPoint: A pipeline makes every prospect's next action visible. Stage names should reflect what has happened, not what you assume about the prospect. Assign owners, test movement, and keep the pipeline current. A pipeline that is not updated is worse than no pipeline at all.

actionSteps.title: Create the Pipeline
actionSteps.description: Navigate to Opportunities → Pipelines and create a new pipeline for discovery calls.

actionSteps.title: Define Stages
actionSteps.description: Add stages: New Enquiry, Call Booked, Call Completed, Proposal Sent, Won/Lost.

actionSteps.title: Assign Owners
actionSteps.description: Name the person responsible for moving prospects through each stage.

actionSteps.title: Test Movement
actionSteps.description: Create a test opportunity and move it through all stages to confirm the flow works.

quizzes.question: Where do you create pipeline stages?

options.option_text: Calendars → Calendar Settings
Opportunities → Pipelines
Sites → Forms
Automation → Workflows

quizzes.explanation: Pipeline stages are created in Opportunities → Pipelines. This is where you define the stages that represent your sales process.

quizzes.question: What should pipeline stage names reflect?

options.option_text: The sales rep's confidence level
Assumptions about the prospect's budget
Actions taken, not assumptions about qualification
The prospect's industry or company size

quizzes.explanation: Stage names should reflect actions taken: Call Booked, Call Completed, Proposal Sent. Avoid assumptions like Hot Lead or Qualified. Actions are factual; assumptions are guesses.

quizzes.question: Why is it important to assign stage owners?

options.option_text: To track who created the opportunity
To calculate commission automatically
To ensure someone is responsible for moving prospects forward
To limit who can view the pipeline

quizzes.explanation: Assigning owners ensures someone is responsible for updating stages and taking next actions. A pipeline without ownership becomes outdated and useless.

title: Connect Booking to the Opportunity
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Add new appointments to the correct pipeline automatically using workflows.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Automation → Workflows → Create Workflow

items.title: Trigger
items.description: Customer Booked Appointment, filtered to your discovery call calendar.

items.title: Action
items.description: Create Opportunity, select your pipeline and set stage to Call Booked.

items.title: Duplicates
items.description: Check duplicate-opportunity behavior on repeat bookings. One booking should create one opportunity.

items.title: Use Separate Actions
items.description: Prefer current Create Opportunity and Update Opportunity actions rather than the older combined Create/Update action.

items.title: Calendar Filter
items.description: Always filter the trigger to the specific discovery call calendar to avoid creating opportunities from unrelated bookings.

items.title: Test Before Publish
items.description: Run a test booking and verify one opportunity appears in the correct pipeline and stage.

items.title: Internal Notification
items.description: Add an internal email or SMS alert to notify the owner when a new opportunity is created.

items.title: CRM Tag
items.description: Tag the contact for segmentation and follow-up tracking.

items.title: Custom Values
items.description: Store booking details in custom fields for reporting and analysis.

keyPoint: A workflow connects the booking to the pipeline automatically. Use Customer Booked Appointment trigger filtered to your calendar, Create Opportunity action in the Call Booked stage, and test thoroughly before publishing. One booking should create exactly one opportunity. Prefer separate Create and Update actions over the older combined action.

actionSteps.title: Create the Workflow
actionSteps.description: Build a new workflow in Automation → Workflows.

actionSteps.title: Set the Trigger
actionSteps.description: Use Customer Booked Appointment filtered to your discovery call calendar.

actionSteps.title: Add the Action
actionSteps.description: Create Opportunity in your pipeline with stage Call Booked.

actionSteps.title: Test
actionSteps.description: Book a test slot and verify one opportunity appears in the correct pipeline and stage.

nextLessonTitle: Manage the Outcome and Next Move

quizzes.question: What event should start the booking-to-pipeline workflow?

options.option_text: Contact Created
Form Submitted
Opportunity Status Changed
Customer Booked Appointment, filtered to the chosen discovery call calendar

quizzes.explanation: Use Customer Booked Appointment filtered to your specific discovery call calendar. This ensures only bookings from that calendar create opportunities, not appointments from other calendars.

quizzes.question: What action creates a new pipeline card?

options.option_text: Add Tag
Create Opportunity, with pipeline and initial stage selected
Send Email
Update Contact

quizzes.explanation: Create Opportunity is the action that adds a new card to your pipeline. You must select the correct pipeline and initial stage (typically Call Booked for discovery calls).

quizzes.question: Why should you prefer separate Create Opportunity and Update Opportunity actions?

options.option_text: They are newer and look better
They are required for all new accounts
The older combined action is being removed
They give clearer control over when opportunities are created vs updated

quizzes.explanation: Separate Create and Update actions give you clearer control. You know exactly when a new opportunity is created versus when an existing one is updated. This prevents confusion and duplicate records.

title: Manage the Outcome and Next Move
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Ensure no booking disappears after its scheduled time with appropriate follow-up for every outcome.

items.title: Attended
items.description: Call happened. Follow up with recap, agreed next action, and move opportunity to Call Completed or Proposal Sent.

items.title: No-Show
items.description: Prospect did not attend. Send polite rebook invitation. Do not treat as cancellation.

items.title: Rescheduled
items.description: Call moved to new time. Update appointment, confirm new details, and adjust reminders.

items.title: Cancelled
items.description: Call cancelled by prospect. Stop pre-call reminders. Update opportunity status. Consider gentle follow-up later.

items.title: Not a Fit
items.description: Call happened but prospect is not suitable. Update stage to Lost with reason. Be polite and helpful.

items.title: Menu Path
items.description: Automation → Workflows → Appointment Status trigger

items.title: Trigger
items.description: Appointment Status changes: Showed, No-show, Cancelled.

items.title: Actions
items.description: Update opportunity stage, send appropriate message, and assign next task.

items.title: Find the Right Opportunity
items.description: When updating from a non-opportunity trigger, find the correct opportunity first before updating.

items.title: No-Show vs Cancellation
items.description: A no-show is not the same as a cancellation. Different statuses require different responses.

items.title: Reschedule vs New Booking
items.description: Rescheduling updates the existing appointment. A new booking creates a new appointment and potentially a new opportunity.

items.title: Document Everything
items.description: Record outcomes, reasons, and next actions on the opportunity and contact record.

keyPoint: Every booking must have a post-appointment status and action. Attended calls get recaps and next steps. No-shows get rebook invitations. Cancellations stop reminders. Not-a-fit gets polite closure. Use Appointment Status workflows to automate these responses and keep your pipeline current.

actionSteps.title: Define Responses
actionSteps.description: Write one next action for each of the five outcomes.

actionSteps.title: Build Status Workflow
actionSteps.description: Create an Appointment Status workflow to handle showed, no-show, and cancelled statuses.

actionSteps.title: Test Each Path
actionSteps.description: Simulate each outcome and verify the correct message sends and opportunity updates.

quizzes.question: Should a no-show be treated the same as a cancellation?

options.option_text: No, they are different statuses requiring different responses
Yes, both should receive the same follow-up message
No, but only cancellations need follow-up
Yes, they are the same thing

quizzes.explanation: A no-show and cancellation are different. A no-show may still be interested and needs a polite rebook invitation. A cancellation may indicate disinterest and needs different handling. Treat them as separate statuses.

quizzes.question: What trigger handles post-appointment status changes?

options.option_text: Opportunity Created
Form Submitted
Appointment Status
Customer Booked Appointment

quizzes.explanation: The Appointment Status trigger fires when an appointment status changes to Showed, No-show, or Cancelled. Use this to automate post-appointment follow-up and pipeline updates.

quizzes.question: What should you do when a non-opportunity trigger needs to update a deal?

options.option_text: Find the right opportunity first, then update that record
Create a new opportunity every time
Update all opportunities for that contact
Skip the update and handle it manually

quizzes.explanation: When a non-opportunity trigger needs to update a deal, first find the correct opportunity for that contact, then update that specific record. This prevents creating duplicates or updating the wrong deal.

title: End-to-End Test and Publish
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Prove the whole experience works before sharing publicly.

items.title: Public Page
items.description: Booking URL loads correctly on mobile and desktop.

items.title: Form Capture
items.description: Qualification form appears after slot selection and answers save to contact record.

items.title: Calendar Booking
items.description: Appointment appears on the correct calendar with right time and details.

items.title: One Confirmation
items.description: Exactly one confirmation message arrives with correct details.

items.title: Reminders
items.description: Reminder emails are scheduled for correct times.

items.title: Opportunity
items.description: One opportunity created in the correct pipeline and stage.

items.title: No Duplicates
items.description: No duplicate messages or opportunities created.

items.title: Use a New Test Contact
items.description: Create a fresh test contact with an email you can check. Do not use your admin account.

items.title: Pick a Test Slot
items.description: Choose a time far enough in the future to allow reminder testing.

items.title: Complete the Form
items.description: Answer all qualification questions and submit the booking.

items.title: Inspect Everything
items.description: Check contact record, appointment, messages, workflow logs, and opportunity.

items.title: Test Cancellation/No-Show
items.description: Simulate these statuses and verify correct follow-up actions.

items.title: Review Workflow Logs
items.description: Check that workflows fired correctly and actions completed.

items.title: Verify Email Delivery
items.description: Confirm messages arrived and contain correct merge field values.

items.title: Fix Issues
items.description: Repair any failed steps before sharing the booking link publicly.

items.title: Publish Workflows
items.description: Only publish workflows after testing is acceptable.

keyPoint: A booking system that is not tested is a liability. Use a fresh test contact, complete the full journey, inspect every touchpoint, and fix issues before publishing. Test cancellation and no-show paths too. Publish workflows only after the test is acceptable.

actionSteps.title: Create Test Contact
actionSteps.description: Set up a new test contact with an email you can monitor.

actionSteps.title: Complete Test Booking
actionSteps.description: Book a slot, answer the form, and verify every step.

actionSteps.title: Inspect Results
actionSteps.description: Check contact record, appointment, messages, opportunity, and workflow logs.

actionSteps.title: Fix and Publish
actionSteps.description: Repair any issues, then publish workflows and share the link.

nextLessonTitle: Put the Booking Link to Work

quizzes.question: What should you use for testing the booking system?

options.option_text: A new test contact with an email you can check
A real prospect's contact details
No testing is needed if the setup looks correct
Your admin account

quizzes.explanation: Always use a fresh test contact with an email you can monitor. Your admin account may bypass certain triggers or notifications. Real prospects should never be used for testing.

quizzes.question: What should you verify before publishing workflows?

options.option_text: That the workflow is named correctly
That all merge fields are available in the account
That the test booking succeeds without duplicate messages or opportunities
That the workflow has at least five actions

quizzes.explanation: Publish workflows only after testing shows the complete booking journey works: one confirmation, correct reminders, one opportunity, no duplicates. An untested workflow can damage your reputation.

quizzes.question: Why should you test cancellation and no-show paths?

options.option_text: They are required by data protection laws
To verify correct follow-up actions and message content
To reduce the number of bookings you receive
They are the most common outcomes

quizzes.explanation: Testing cancellation and no-show paths verifies that the correct follow-up messages send, opportunities update properly, and no inappropriate reminders continue. These edge cases reveal system gaps.

title: Put the Booking Link to Work
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Drive relevant conversations by placing the booking link where prospects will find it.

items.title: Email Signature
items.description: Add a subtle CTA to your email signature for every outgoing message.

items.title: Website CTA
items.description: Place on relevant pages: services, about, or contact. Not every page.

items.title: Social Bio / DM
items.description: Link in bio or direct message for interested connections.

items.title: Post-Event Follow-Up
items.description: After speaking, training, or networking, send a tailored follow-up with the booking link.

items.title: QR Code
items.description: Print on business cards, handouts, or presentation slides for in-person events.

items.title: Speaker
items.description: Want to discuss your next speaking event? Book a 30-minute enquiry call.

items.title: Coach
items.description: Ready to explore coaching? Let's talk about your goals. Book a fit call.

items.title: Consultant
items.description: Struggling with systems? Book a discovery call to map your friction points.

items.title: Service Business
items.description: Need an estimate? Book a 30-minute call to discuss your project.

items.title: Generic Broadcasts
items.description: Don't send booking links to everyone. Target people who have shown interest or fit your audience.

items.title: Misleading CTAs
items.description: Don't promise a free strategy session when it is a 30-minute discovery call. Set honest expectations.

items.title: Context Matters
items.description: The link should appear where the prospect is already thinking about the problem you solve.

keyPoint: A booking link that nobody sees is useless. Place it where interested prospects already are: email signatures, relevant website pages, social bios, post-event follow-ups, and QR codes. Write contextual CTAs that match the prospect's situation. Never spam generic booking requests.

actionSteps.title: Pick Three Channels
actionSteps.description: Choose three places to share your booking link based on where your prospects spend time.

actionSteps.title: Write Contextual CTAs
actionSteps.description: Create one-line calls-to-action that match each channel and audience.

actionSteps.title: Add and Test
actionSteps.description: Add the links to your chosen channels and test that they work on mobile and desktop.

quizzes.question: Where should you place your booking link?

options.option_text: In every email you send, regardless of topic
Every page of your website and all social media posts
Where interested prospects already are, with contextual CTAs
Only on a dedicated landing page

quizzes.explanation: Place the booking link where interested prospects already spend time: email signatures, relevant website pages, social bios, post-event follow-ups. Context matters more than volume.

quizzes.question: What should your CTA say?

options.option_text: Click here to book now!
Book before prices go up
Free consultation — limited time only!
A contextual message that matches the prospect's situation and need

quizzes.explanation: Contextual CTAs match the prospect's situation. Want to discuss your next speaking event? Book a 30-minute enquiry call. This is more effective than generic urgency tactics.

quizzes.question: What should you avoid when sharing your booking link?

options.option_text: Testing the link before sharing
Sending generic booking requests to everyone
Writing different CTAs for different audiences
Using multiple channels

quizzes.explanation: Avoid sending generic booking requests to everyone. Target people who have shown interest or fit your audience. Spam damages your reputation and wastes your time on unqualified calls.

title: Measure and Improve
moduleName: Build a Discovery Call Booking System
learningGoal: Review bookings and outcomes weekly, then make one targeted improvement.

items.title: Bookings
items.description: How many discovery calls were booked this week?

items.title: Show-ups
items.description: How many booked prospects actually attended?

items.title: Completed Next Steps
items.description: How many calls led to a clear next action: proposal, follow-up, or close?

items.title: Booked-to-Show Rate
items.description: Percentage of bookings that result in attended calls.

items.title: Booked-to-Qualified Rate
items.description: Percentage of attended calls that lead to a viable next step.

items.title: Schedule the Review
items.description: Block 15 minutes weekly to review metrics and identify one improvement.

items.title: Count the Numbers
items.description: Record bookings, show-ups, and completed next steps.

items.title: Identify Patterns
items.description: Are no-shows increasing? Are certain channels driving better prospects?

items.title: Pick One Improvement
items.description: Choose one change to test: better reminder timing, different CTA, revised qualification questions.

items.title: Assign an Owner
items.description: Someone must own the system, review metrics, and make improvements.

items.title: Record the Link
items.description: Document the live booking URL, owner, and review schedule.

items.title: Set Review Date
items.description: Schedule the first review and recurring weekly reviews.

items.title: Celebrate
items.description: A working booking system is a genuine business asset. Acknowledge the achievement.

keyPoint: A booking system that is not reviewed becomes outdated. Count bookings, show-ups, and next steps weekly. Identify patterns, pick one improvement, and test it. Assign an owner and schedule recurring reviews. A system that evolves based on data will consistently outperform a system that is set up once and forgotten.

actionSteps.title: Record Baseline
actionSteps.description: Document current bookings, show-ups, and next steps for the past week.

actionSteps.title: Schedule Reviews
actionSteps.description: Block 15 minutes weekly for system review and improvement.

actionSteps.title: Pick One Test
actionSteps.description: Choose one improvement to test: reminder timing, CTA wording, or qualification questions.

actionSteps.title: Assign Owner
actionSteps.description: Name the person responsible for metrics, review, and updates.

quizzes.question: What are three basic metrics to track weekly?

options.option_text: Revenue, profit margin, and customer lifetime value
Video views, blog comments, and podcast downloads
Bookings, show-ups, and completed next steps
Website traffic, social media followers, email open rates

quizzes.explanation: The three basic metrics are bookings (how many calls scheduled), show-ups (how many attended), and completed next steps (how many led to action). These tell you if the system is working.

quizzes.question: What should you do at each weekly review?

options.option_text: Compare your metrics to competitor benchmarks
Redesign the entire booking system
Hire a consultant to optimize the system
Count numbers, identify patterns, and pick one improvement to test

quizzes.explanation: At each review, count the numbers, look for patterns, and choose one improvement to test. Small, consistent improvements compound over time. Major redesigns are rarely needed.

quizzes.question: Why is system ownership important?

options.option_text: To limit who can use the booking system
To assign blame when things go wrong
To ensure someone is responsible for review, metrics, and improvement
To increase the cost of the system

quizzes.explanation: An owner ensures the system is reviewed, metrics are tracked, and improvements are made. A system without ownership becomes outdated and ineffective. Ownership is about accountability, not blame.
